content.title: About
content.content: Light spinach dip is a smooth sauce made from fresh spinach, low‑fat cottage cheese and gentle spices. It has a mild, slightly tangy flavor and creamy texture, perfect for diet‑friendly meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Spinach is rich in iron, vitamin K and folate, making it a staple of healthy eating.
Light dips often replace cream with cottage cheese or yogurt, reducing calories.
Spinach dip is commonly used in Mediterranean cuisine as a sauce for vegetables and seafood.
The sodium content in light versions is usually lower than in traditional mayonnaise‑based sauces.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Spinach provides lutein and zeaxanthin, which support eye health.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C and vitamin A in spinach help strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Low‑calorie protein source
items.content: Cottage cheese adds animal protein without excess fat.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Fiber from spinach promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Cholesterol reduction
items.content: Low saturated fat content helps maintain healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cottage cheese may trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Spinach contains oxalates, which in large amounts can contribute to kidney stone formation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some ready‑made versions add salt; those monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dip with fresh vegetables, whole‑grain crackers, or use it as a sauce for fish and chicken. It also works well in sandwiches or as a salad dressing.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the dip in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
